question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int 3\sin\left(3 - 7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}} $+C$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3 - 7 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-7,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{1}{7}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 3\sin\left(3 - 7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=3\left(- \frac{1}{7}\right)\int \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{7}\int \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{7}\left(-\cos\left(u\right)\right)+C\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\cos\left(3 - 7 x\right)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}} 9\sin\left(9 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=9 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=9,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=9\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{\pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=9\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}} 9\sin\left(9 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=9\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ &=-1\left(\cos\left(\pi\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=-1\left(\left(-1\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\\ &=2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\int 4\cos\left(1 - 5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=1 - 5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{1}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 4\cos\left(1 - 5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=4\left(- \frac{1}{5}\right)\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{4}{5}\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{4}{5}\left(\sin\left(u\right)\right)+C\\ &=- \frac{4}{5}\sin\left(1 - 5 x\right)+C.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{10}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{5}} 6\cos\left(5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3 \pi}{10}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(\frac{3 \pi}{10}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\\ x=\frac{2 \pi}{5}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(\frac{2 \pi}{5}\right)+\left(0\right)=2 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{10}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{5}} 6\cos\left(5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=6\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\sin\left(2 \pi\right)-\sin\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\left(0\right)-\left(-1\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{6}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{\pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} 8\sin\left(6 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{12}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{6}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} 8\sin\left(6 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=8\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\\ &=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\cos\left(\pi\right)-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\left(-1\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int 2\cos\left(2 x + 6\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 x + 6.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2\cos\left(2 x + 6\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left(\sin\left(u\right)\right)+C\\ &=\sin\left(2 x + 6\right)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
